root_cause: The heavy lease root used os.tmpdir(), which follows TMPDIR. The approved external release profile and the default shell therefore reserved distinct heavy directories for the same user and host.

original_path_evidence.result: Two independent mkdir heavy reservations were possible. No workload was launched to reproduce the split.

repair: Use /var/tmp/matrx-stabilization-resource-<uid> for all new admissions. Before preflight, fail closed when a known old TMPDIR lease or unsafe hold remains, when another old runner exists, or when a detached resource-owned process exists. The documented external TMPDIR is registered as a legacy root; its state is inspected from a default TMPDIR invocation. Existing legacy state is never removed by the new guard.

red_green.red: The default-TMPDIR legacy discovery test failed before adding the external legacy root to the policy (3 pass, 1 fail).
red_green.green: All four focused tests pass (4 pass, 0 fail).

bounded_integration.scope: Two check-mode processes only; no build, browser, or test workload.
bounded_integration.first: Default TMPDIR check created /var/tmp/matrx-stabilization-resource-501/heavy/owner.json and held the preflight.
bounded_integration.second: External TMPDIR check exited 2 with RESOURCE_HEAVY_BUSY before sampling or launching work.
bounded_integration.first_exit: After the full 60-second preflight, the first check emitted RESOURCE_ADMITTED with reasons=[] and exited 0; its heavy owner file was released.

verification_limits: The check-mode probe verifies cross-TMPDIR admission. It does not certify extension behavior. The legacy bridge covers registered previous TMPDIRs, live old runners, and discoverable owner-token descendants; it does not claim indefinite compatibility with a separately started old script copy after its census or infer an unknown dead legacy root on an arbitrary volume. Independent review and final source reconciliation remain with the root owner.
